questions.q: What was the name of the steamer Fix was waiting for at Suez?
choices: The Mongolia
The Rangoon
The Carnatic
The Henrietta
questions.evidence: the arrival of the steamer Mongolia

questions.q: What was Fix's job at Suez?
choices: To deliver the Indian mails to the steamer
To watch every arriving passenger for the bank robber
To sign and seal the passports of English travellers
To guard the coal supply for ships on the canal
questions.evidence: it was his task to narrowly watch every passenger who arrived at Suez

questions.q: What seems to drive Fix most in his hunt for the thief?
choices: Hope of the splendid reward
Anger at losing his own money to the robber
A promise he made to the Bank's directors
Orders from the British consul at Suez
questions.evidence: inspired by the hope of obtaining the splendid reward

questions.q: How did Fix say a good detective recognises a thief?
choices: By studying photographs sent from Scotland Yard
By feeling the thief's presence, like a sixth sense
By checking every passport for a forged signature
By watching for anyone who seems nervous or afraid
questions.evidence: A man rather feels the presence of these fellows, consul, than recognises them.

questions.q: The consul warns Fix that the description "has a singular resemblance to an honest man." What is the consul suggesting?
choices: The description fits Fix himself very closely
The thief has surely changed his clothes and face
The description might fit many innocent men
The Bank has sent the wrong description by mistake
questions.evidence: has a singular resemblance to an honest man

questions.q: "Mr. Fix evidently was not wanting in a tinge of self-conceit." What does this tell us about Fix?
choices: He was rather proud of himself
He had no confidence at all in his own skills
He wanted very badly to go back home to London
He was shy and did not like to talk about himself
questions.evidence: Mr. Fix evidently was not wanting in a tinge of self-conceit.

questions.q: How long would the Mongolia stop at Suez, and why?
choices: One day, so the passengers could see the town
Four hours, which is long enough to take on coal
Two days, while the Indian mails were sorted
Six hours, to wait for the tide in the canal
questions.evidence: Four hours; long enough to get in her coal.

questions.q: What surprised Fix when a passenger showed him a passport on the quay?
choices: It belonged to a member of the Reform Club
It had already been stamped by the English consul
Its description matched that of the bank robber
It was written entirely in the French language
questions.evidence: the description in the passport was identical with that of the bank robber

questions.q: What did the passenger with the passport do after Fix told him where the consulate was?
choices: He went straight to the consulate by himself
He went back to the steamer to fetch his master
He asked Fix to come along and show him the way
He gave the passport to Fix to take to the consul
questions.evidence: I'll go and fetch my master

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: Fogg and Passepartout touring the town of Suez
The building of the great canal by M. Lesseps
The detective Fix eagerly waiting for the steamer to find his thief
The consul arresting a suspicious passenger
questions.evidence: awaited with a feverish impatience, easy to understand, the arrival of the steamer Mongolia
